title: Best Design Agencies for YC Startups (2026)
description: Eight design agencies for YC startups, each with YC clients we checked in YC's directory, compared by stage and price, from $1,490/mo to $50k+. Ours: $15k.

body.x: The best design agencies for YC startups split by how far past Demo Day you are. In the batch, Awesomic ($1,490–2,995 a month) or Designjoy ($4,995 a month) covers launch work, and at seed Zypsy trades design for equity. After the Series A, PIXELUP LABS ships a $15k brand sprint in 2–4 weeks for teams going enterprise, and past the Series B, MetaLab and Clay list minimums from $50,000.

"Backed by YC" is not a brand. It's a line every company in the batch can print. Two years after Demo Day, enterprise buyers stop judging your product and start judging whether you'll exist in three years.
This list is for YC companies at that point: Series A raised, first enterprise AE hired, a site that still reads like the batch. It also tells founders still in the batch what to skip.
Every studio below names at least two YC companies as clients on its own website. We looked up each one in YC's company directory on October 7, 2026.

body.x: Methodology: how we picked and ordered these design agencies for YC startups

We put 11 design studios through four tests on October 7, 2026, and eight passed. The candidates were the studios that come up when founders search for design help for YC companies, plus the studios we already compare on our other lists.
The four tests. Every studio on this list passed all of them:

items: It names at least two YC companies on its own website, in a case study, work page, logo wall, or testimonial, and each one is in YC's directory. One name wasn't enough.
It operates under its own name today.
It has a public price signal, or one reported by a directory and labeled that way.
It wins a stage or a job no other entry wins, and we could say where it's the wrong choice. An entry with no weakness is an ad.

body.x: How we checked YC clients. A YC client here means a company in YC's company directory, listed with its batch: W24 is Winter 2024, S21 is Summer 2021, F24 is Fall 2024. We looked up studios' named clients in YC's directory and recorded the batch of each match. Unnamed logos and "YC-backed founders" with no company attached didn't count.

What we compared. For each studio we recorded six things: stage fit, named YC clients, price and its source, published timeline, engagement model, and where it's the wrong choice. We didn't add them into a score.

Where the facts come from. Prices come from each studio's own pages, its Clutch and DesignRush listings, or press coverage, and every competitor entry prints its check date. We haven't hired any of these studios, so each "where it doesn't" comes from their public pages and listings. Other agencies' lists only helped us find names.

How we ordered the list. PIXELUP LABS is first because this is our list. The other seven run in stage order, from the batch to late stage, since budgets grow from YC's $500,000 check onward. They aren't ranked against each other: number two isn't better than number eight.

What changes the list. A studio that names a second YC client can move on, and one that stops operating under its own name moves off. The three studios that failed a test are named in the cut list, each with its reason.
How we know this market

We have run 31 projects for funded B2B and AI-native startups, with 5.0★ across every review. Eleven of our clients are YC companies: Greptile (W24, for its 2025 rebrand and design system), Reducto (W24), Monumint (W24), Sully (S21), Bland AI (S23), CTGT (F24), Revyl (F24), Dayflow (S24), Synthio Labs (Spring 2025), Autumn (S25), and Audrion (F25).
That doesn't make us neutral. It does make us familiar with the moment a YC company outgrows its Demo Day site. Our Brand Sprint price is public on Contra, so you can rule us out before a call.
What does design cost a YC startup in 2026?

Design for a YC startup costs $0 to $50,000 and up, depending on stage. In the batch, most teams should spend $0 on a template or $1,490–4,995 a month on a subscription. After the Series A, brand plus website runs $25–40k at a sprint studio, Ramotion's brand package alone is $60,000, and MetaLab and Clay start at $50,000.

YC's standard deal is the yardstick. YC invests $500,000: $125,000 for a fixed 7%, and $375,000 on an uncapped MFN SAFE. A $15k brand sprint would take 3% of that check, which is why most teams in the batch should wait.
A brand sprint is a fixed-scope project that ships positioning and a visual identity in weeks, not a retainer that runs for months.

What it is. PIXELUP LABS is the enterprise-readiness design partner for funded B2B startups, most of them AI-native. We're a 7-person studio in San Francisco, with the production studio in Bangalore, and we ship positioning, brand, website, and product design as one argument.

YC clients we checked. Greptile (W24, the 2025 rebrand and design system), Reducto (W24), Monumint (W24), Sully (S21), Bland AI (S23), CTGT (F24), Revyl (F24), Dayflow (S24), Synthio Labs (Spring 2025), and Autumn (S25). Audrion (F25) has no YC directory page to check.

Where it shines. The moment after the Series A when the product has moved upmarket and the brand hasn't. At that point the YC logo isn't the flex. A brand buyers recognize before they read the name is.
Greptile's 2025 rebrand and design system turned "we find bugs in your codebase" into a green lizard that kills bugs, backed by 200+ components with developer-first docs.

Sully's website redesign became a sales-enablement project, because that was the real problem. Monumint went from kickoff to a public rebrand and one-page site in seven weeks, and Synthio Labs put our pace this way: "they get timelines, a rarity!"
Where it doesn't. In the batch, $15k is 3% of YC's $500,000 check, and most teams should spend it on the product. If you're still pivoting, there's no opinion for us to build a brand around yet.

MetaLab is the better hire for product design plus engineering at scale. For interactive craft aimed at developers, basement.studio wins, and Clay wins an enterprise brand program with a committee. We're not a growth agency either: we fix how you're perceived, not how many leads you buy.
Price and timeline. Brand sprint $15k in 2–4 weeks, brand plus website $25–40k in 6–8 weeks, and a retainer from $6k/mo. Our Brand Sprint is listed on Contra.
Verdict. Hire us when you've raised the A, hired the first enterprise AE, and procurement has started asking how long you've been around. Most teams shouldn't hire us just for Demo Day.
2. Awesomic: best for design capacity during the batch
Awesomic homepage, captured September 25, 2026 · awesomic.com
What it is. Awesomic is a YC company itself (S21): a subscription that matches startups with vetted designers, developers, and no-coders, usually within 24 hours.
YC clients we checked. Pylon (W23) and Fondo (W18). Both founders give testimonials on Awesomic's homepage, and several more testimonials there carry YC batch badges.

Where it shines. Speed at a batch budget. In a testimonial on that homepage, Playhouse co-founder Nathan Shinder says Awesomic built the company's Webflow landing page and it "went live in a matter of days."

Where it doesn't. Judging by its public pages, you buy matched talent by the month, not a team that owns your positioning. The plans sell design, copy, and Webflow capacity, so the strategy has to come from you.

Price and timeline. Awesomic publishes $1,490/mo for Graphic Pack, $2,995/mo for All-in-One (copy, design, and Webflow), and $200/mo for its AI design product, monthly with no commitment (checked September 30, 2026). Quarterly plans save 20%.
Verdict. Hire Awesomic in the batch when you need a landing page, a deck, and launch graphics this month, and you can write the brief yourself.
3. Designjoy: best for a steady queue of design requests
Designjoy homepage, captured September 25, 2026 · designjoy.co
What it is. Designjoy is Brett Williams' productized design subscription: one senior designer, no account layer, one active request at a time.
YC clients we checked. Webflow (S13) and Product Hunt (S14), both on the logo wall on Designjoy's homepage. The logos don't say what the work was.
Where it shines. Taste and predictability. The price is public, most requests come back in two business days on average, and you can pause or cancel anytime.

Where it doesn't. One request at a time is also the ceiling. A brand, a site, a deck, and a product surface can't move in parallel, and the work list (websites, logos, UI, Webflow, brand guides, decks, ads) doesn't include positioning.
Price and timeline. Designjoy publishes $4,995/mo, discounted from $5,995 (checked October 7, 2026).
Verdict. Hire Designjoy when the story is settled and you need one good designer working through a queue every week.
4. Zypsy: best when you have more equity than cash
Zypsy homepage, captured October 7, 2026 · zypsy.com
What it is. Zypsy describes itself as a design team for founders, with an investment arm. It was founded in 2018 and does brand, product, and engineering work.
YC clients we checked. Podium (W16) and Cortex (W20), both on Zypsy's work page.

Where it shines. Paying in equity. Its Design Capital program, as TechCrunch reported in April 2024, trades $100,000 of brand and product design for 1% equity on a SAFE, over 8 to 10 weeks. Zypsy wins only if you do.

Where it doesn't. Equity is the most expensive currency a winning company has: 1% of a $1 billion company is $10 million. Eight to ten weeks also won't fit a Demo Day six weeks out, and TechCrunch reported that work beyond the program's scope moves to a cash retainer.

Price and timeline. Zypsy's site doesn't list current Design Capital terms (checked October 7, 2026), so treat the 2024 figures as a reported signal. For cash projects, its Clutch profile lists a $50,000+ minimum.
Verdict. Hire Zypsy at seed when runway is tighter than your cap table and you want a design partner paid in the same currency as your investors.
5. basement.studio: best for developer-facing brand and web craft
basement.studio homepage, captured September 25, 2026 · basement.studio
What it is. basement.studio is a design and engineering studio based in Mar del Plata, Argentina. Its FAQ lists Vercel, Cursor, Harvey AI, ElevenLabs, and Scale AI among its clients.
YC clients we checked. Scale AI (S16), "A Partnership Built for Growth" (2025), and Mintlify (W22), "Documentation, Reimagined" (2026). Both are on its showcase.
Where it shines. The visual language engineers respect. If your buyer is a developer, a basement site says you belong in the same room as Vercel and Cursor.

Where it doesn't. Judging by its public work, basement is a craft and web studio more than a positioning shop. If you can't state your category claim yet, strong execution makes an unclear idea louder.

Price and timeline. basement publishes no price on its site or FAQ (checked October 7, 2026). Reported Clutch figures put the minimum at $10,000 and hourly rates at $100–149. We couldn't find a live profile to confirm them, so treat them as a reported signal, not a quote.
Verdict. Hire basement when you sell to developers, your positioning is settled, and you want the craft your buyers' engineers already admire.
6. Ramotion: best for brand and product UI from one team, at a published price
Ramotion homepage, captured September 25, 2026 · ramotion.com
What it is. Ramotion calls itself a product and brand design agency, with offices in San Francisco, New York, and Los Angeles. It was founded in 2009, and its About page lists 70 team experts.

YC clients we checked. Stripe (S09) and Truebill (W16, now Rocket Money), both on its work page. Ramotion says it did Truebill's branding and UI/UX, then came back to refresh the brand as Truebill grew past subscription management.
Where it shines. Work where brand identity and product UI carry equal weight. The price is published, which MetaLab, Clay, and basement.studio don't do.
Where it doesn't. The brand packages take 3.5 months and price the website separately, so brand plus a 1–5 page site runs $85,000–120,000. That's not a sprint before a funding announcement.

Price and timeline. Ramotion's startup packages list Brand Creation at $60,000 and Brand Redesign at $85,000, each 3.5 months, plus $25,000–60,000 for a 1–5 page website (checked October 7, 2026). Its Brand Team Extension runs $9,500 a month part-time, with a three-month minimum.

Verdict. Hire Ramotion at Series A or B when the brand and the product UI need one team and you'd rather buy a published package than wait for a quote. Our Ramotion alternatives page covers faster and cheaper routes.
7. MetaLab: best for growth-stage product design and engineering
MetaLab homepage, captured September 25, 2026 · metalab.com
What it is. MetaLab is a product design and engineering studio founded in 2006 in Victoria, BC. Its teams are "100% dedicated to a single client," and it has shipped more than 475 products.
YC clients we checked. Coinbase (S12), Instacart (S12), and Webflow (S13), all on its work page. For Coinbase, MetaLab designed and built the marketing site that introduced Bitcoin to new buyers.
Where it shines. Complex software with a lot of surface area. A dedicated team designs and builds next to yours, which is what a Series B product adding new user types needs.
Where it doesn't. It's priced and staffed for scale. A brand-and-site sprint before a funding announcement is a small job for a studio with a $100,000 Clutch minimum.
Price and timeline. MetaLab publishes no prices. DesignRush lists "$50,000 & Up" and Clutch a $100,000+ minimum (both checked September 30, 2026). No timeline is published.
Verdict. Hire MetaLab after the Series B, when the product is the hard part and you want design and engineering from one team. Our MetaLab alternatives page covers the cheaper routes.
8. Clay: best for an enterprise brand program at late stage
Clay homepage, captured September 25, 2026 · clay.global

What it is. Clay is a San Francisco brand, UI/UX, and digital agency with offices in New York, Austin, Denver, Lisbon, and Belgrade. Its services run from brand strategy and identity to product design and full development.
YC clients we checked. Stripe (S09) and Coinbase (S12), both on its work page, Coinbase in the archive.

Where it shines. Programs with many stakeholders. On Clay's Clutch profile, 70% of clients are enterprises with more than $1 billion in revenue. A brand program that spans product, web, and several teams is its home ground.
Where it doesn't. A $50,000 minimum and $150–199 an hour assume an enterprise budget and timeline. A Series A team that needs a brand before a funding announcement isn't the job Clay is shaped for.
Price and timeline. Clutch lists a $50,000+ minimum and $150–199 an hour (checked September 25, 2026). No timeline is published.
Verdict. Hire Clay at late stage, when the brand program spans product, web, and several teams. Our Clay agency alternatives page covers smaller budgets.
Studios we cut, and why
Three studios we considered failed one of our tests: at least two named YC clients, or operating under their own name today. Here is why, so you can check our work.

Zyner sells a $9,000 or $14,000 brand-and-site sprint in 2–3 weeks, built for founders in YC and a16z speedrun before Demo Day. Its site names one YC founder, Manil Lakabi (F24), and its homepage client list gives descriptions and funding amounts but no company names, so it fails test 1. If you're in the batch, it's still worth a call.

Parallel is a product design studio whose case-study page lists 34 active clients. The only one we could match in YC's directory is Gullak (S22). Its homepage says engagements "typically start at $10k."
Character fails test 2. It was acquired by Dentsu in 2018 and now operates as part of Dentsu Creative.
Which design agency should a YC startup hire at each stage?

A YC startup should hire a design agency by stage, not by logo. In the batch, spend almost nothing, and at seed, buy capacity or trade equity. After the Series A, pay for positioning and a system; after the Series B, pay for scale.
In the batch, still pivoting. Hire nobody. Ship a template with Claude Code and keep it easy to change. Fall 2026 Demo Day is December 2, and a sharp homepage matters more than a logo.
In the batch, story settled. Awesomic or Designjoy for the landing page, the deck, and launch graphics. Zyner also sells a $9,000 Demo Day sprint, though it names only one YC client.
Seed, more equity than runway. Zypsy.
Series A raised, first enterprise AE, procurement asking how long you've been around. PIXELUP LABS. Our guide to looking enterprise-ready covers what to fix first.
Selling to developers, positioning settled. basement.studio.
Brand and product UI from one team, on a published package. Ramotion.
Series B and later. MetaLab when the product is the hard part. Clay when the brand program spans teams. If the marketing site is the whole job, see our list of SaaS web design agencies.
Hire for the stage you're in, not the one on your pitch deck.
FAQ
Which design firms are known for supporting fast-moving YC teams?

Awesomic and Designjoy move fastest for teams in the batch. Awesomic matches a designer in about 24 hours, and Designjoy returns most requests in two business days. For a full brand and website after the Series A, PIXELUP LABS ships in 6–8 weeks and has worked with 11 YC companies, from Sully (S21) to Audrion (F25). Every studio on this list names at least two YC clients we checked in YC's directory.
Who do Y Combinator founders hire for product design?

It depends on the stage. MetaLab lists Coinbase (S12), Instacart (S12), and Webflow (S13) among its clients and fits growth-stage products. Ramotion pairs product UI with brand, as it did for Truebill (W16). Earlier, Zypsy does brand and product work for equity, and Awesomic matches designers by the month from $1,490.
Who offers strong branding and product design for YC-backed companies?

Zypsy, Ramotion, and MetaLab all cover brand and product: Zypsy for seed teams paying in equity, Ramotion on published packages from $60,000, MetaLab for growth-stage budgets of $50,000+. PIXELUP LABS covers brand, website, and product design for YC companies after the Series A, from a $15k brand sprint. Clay covers both at enterprise scale.
We're going through YC and need a credible brand identity fast. Which agencies work at that speed and budget?

In the batch, Awesomic ($1,490–2,995 a month) and Designjoy ($4,995 a month) fit the budget and the clock. Zyner sells a $9,000 Demo Day brand-and-site sprint in 2–3 weeks, though its site names only one YC client. If your positioning is still moving, a template is the honest answer before Demo Day.
Where should a YC founder look for senior product design support?

Look for studios that name YC clients, then check each name in YC's company directory, as we did on October 7, 2026. MetaLab dedicates each team to a single client, and Zypsy pairs product design with brand. If a studio says it works with YC companies, every name it gives should be in that directory with a batch.
How much should a YC startup spend on design?

In the batch, close to nothing: YC's standard deal is $500,000, and a $15k brand sprint would take 3% of it. After a Series A, $25–40k for brand plus website is a normal range at a sprint studio, and MetaLab or Clay start at $50,000. Our startup rebrand and website cost guide breaks it down by stage.
Should a YC startup rebrand before Demo Day?

Rarely. If the product hasn't found its market, a rebrand can't fix it. In a crowded category, sharpen the positioning and the homepage first, then do the full brand before the Series A. Our guide on rebranding before or after a fundraise covers the timing.
Is trading equity for design work a good deal?

It's cheap if the company stays small and expensive if it wins. Zypsy's Design Capital, as reported in 2024, trades $100,000 of design for 1% on a SAFE, and at a $1 billion outcome that 1% is worth $10 million. YC's standard deal buys a fixed 7% for $125,000, about $17,900 a point.
Do design agencies give YC companies a discount?

Some list deals on Bookface, YC's internal network: a Fondo founder's testimonial on Awesomic's homepage calls it "one of the best deals on bookface." We don't run a YC price. Ours are public: $15k brand sprint (listed on Contra), $25–40k brand plus website, and a retainer from $6k/mo.
Best branding agency for Series A startups

It depends on who buys from you. For a B2B Series A team selling to enterprises, we built PIXELUP LABS for that job: $15k for a brand sprint, $25–40k for brand plus website. For developer buyers, basement.studio fits better, and our B2B branding agencies comparison covers nine options.
Can a YC startup use a template and Claude Code until the Series A?

Yes, while the product is still finding its market. A template costs $0 and changes as fast as your pitch does, which matters more in the batch than a logo. The cost shows up once enterprise buyers start checking you out, and our guide to AI design agencies for startups covers what that sameness costs.
What should a YC founder prepare before hiring a design studio?

Three things: the opinion you hold about your market, the next date that matters (Demo Day, the raise, the first enterprise pilot), and one person who can make decisions. Bring the deck, recent sales calls, and sites you admire. Then ask who maintains the site after launch: we hand over the design system, so brand entropy doesn't set in once we leave.
The bottom line
"Backed by YC" gets you the first meeting. What you look like decides the second one.

title: How Long Does a Startup Rebrand Take? (2026 Timelines)
description: A startup rebrand takes 2–4 weeks for the brand and 6–8 weeks with the website at a sprint studio. Focus Lab and Ramotion take 6 weeks to 5 months.

body.x: A startup rebrand takes 2 to 4 weeks for the brand identity and 6 to 8 weeks with the website when a sprint studio like PIXELUP LABS runs it. Established studios take longer: Focus Lab's engagements run 6 weeks to 5 months, and Ramotion lists 3.5 months for its brand packages. Scope and sign-off set the calendar, not company size.

Nobody asks how long a rebrand takes out of curiosity. Between July and October 2026, Google showed our pages for searches like "a brand refresh timed around a series b announcement." Another asked for "a full visual-verbal identity in eight weeks for our series c announcement." The real question is whether a rebrand fits before your date.

TL;DR: For funded B2B teams, Series A to C, with a date on the calendar. Brand only: 2–4 weeks at a sprint studio, 6 weeks to 3.5 months at an established one. Brand plus website: 6–8 weeks with us, 3–5 months for a structural rebrand at Focus Lab. A separate website specialist adds 12–20 weeks. Count back from your date: a sprint fits inside 8 weeks, a rename or a steering committee usually doesn't.
How long does a startup rebrand take with each type of partner?

A startup rebrand takes from a weekend to six months, depending on who does it. Templates take a weekend, freelancers 2–4 weeks for an identity, and sprint studios 2–8 weeks for brand and site. Established studios take 6 weeks to 5 months.

What fits inside a 2–4 week brand sprint, and what takes 6–8 weeks?

A brand sprint is a fixed-price, fixed-scope engagement that produces positioning and a brand identity in weeks instead of months. At PIXELUP LABS the brand sprint runs 2–4 weeks for $15k. Adding the website takes the project to 6–8 weeks and $25–40k. Rolling the brand into everything else continues after launch.

rows: Brand strategy and positioning, a logo system, a visual identity, brand guidelines, and examples of the brand on your site, deck, social and product
The sprint, plus information architecture, full visual design, motion where it earns its place, a developer-ready handoff, and the build on Framer, Webflow or Next.js

body.x: Shipping fast is not the flex. Shipping fast and leaving nothing to clean up is.

Our sprints are short because the process was built for weeks, not because a five-month process got squeezed. One or two people decide, a small senior team does the work, and every project gets founder creative direction. AI speeds up production. Taste stays human.

What it looked like on Monumint. We ran the full rebrand for Monumint, a fintech, and shipped a one-page site on Framer in 7 weeks from kickoff to public launch. Brand direction and logo locked at about week 4. The client had already chosen the name, so naming sat outside those 7 weeks.
Add product UI, a multi-page build or heavy motion, and the calendar grows. The 6–8 weeks covers brand plus a focused site.
Clients notice. SynthioLabs: "they get timelines, a rarity!" Sully: "super quick turnarounds."
Fast craft is not fast results, though. As I put it on LinkedIn: "if an agency promises to transform your product metrics in a 2-week sprint, RUN."
What makes a startup rebrand take longer?

Five things stretch a startup rebrand: sign-off, research depth, a name change, the number of surfaces, and your own team's speed. Company size matters less than any of them. A Series C with two decision-makers moves faster than a Series A with a committee.

Sign-off. Every extra approver and every extra round adds time. Monumint's contract capped design at 3 revision rounds. Seven written feedback rounds came in before launch. Our own Contra listing says the sprint isn't for: "Anyone who needs 4 logo rounds and committee approval."

Research depth. Customer interviews and a perception study take calendar time no designer can compress. Focus Lab lists "Brand Strategy & Complex Initiatives (12+ weeks)" separately from its 6-week sprint.
A new name. Naming adds legal time on top of design. The USPTO averaged 4.45 months to a first examination action in the first half of fiscal 2026.

Surfaces. The identity is the fast part of a rebrand. The rollout is the slow part. Bynder's 2023 survey of 1,002 marketers found a typical rebrand updates 215 assets over seven months, from first talks to rollout.
Your side of the table. Copy, the customer logos you're allowed to show, and security reviews all run on your team's clock. The launch waits for the slowest one.
When should a startup rebrand take longer than 8 weeks?

A startup rebrand should take longer than 8 weeks when the company is merging brands, changing its name, answering to a steering committee, or rolling out across regions. A sprint is the wrong tool for those. And if you're still finding product-market fit, the right timeline is zero.

items: Pre-PMF or mid-pivot. If you're still finding PMF, don't hire us. Use a template and Claude Code, honestly. Come back after the pivot settles.
A steering committee. We work founder-to-founder. If your rebrand needs a steering committee, a Landor- or Pentagram-tier firm will serve you better.

M&A or several product brands. Focus Lab's Structural Rebrand runs 3–5 months from $25,000 a month and covers M&A integration, brand architecture and multi-brand systems. For a Series C folding in an acquisition, that's the right instrument. We compared the studios around it in Focus Lab alternatives.
A rename. Budget months for trademark work, and start it before design.
A locked strategy. If the strategy is done and locked, a freelancer at $2–8k is cheaper and faster than any studio, us included.

Is a 2 week brand sprint for startups realistic?
For the identity, nearly. PIXELUP LABS runs brand sprints in 2–4 weeks for $15k, covering positioning, a logo system, a visual identity and guidelines. With the website, plan on 6–8 weeks.
How long does a website redesign take after a rebrand?

Website specialists quote 12 to 20 weeks: Huemor 12–16 for a SaaS redesign, Bop Design 16–20, Webstacks 90–120 days. A build from approved designs is faster; TripleDart quotes 1–6 weeks for Figma to Webflow. We do brand and site together in 6–8 weeks, with no hand-off between vendors. Our comparison of SaaS web design agencies has each one’s price and timeline.
How long does a rebrand take for a Series B or Series C company?

As long as its sign-off chain. Our 6–8 weeks for brand plus website assumes one or two people make the calls, whatever the stage. A Series C with a steering committee, a rename or several product brands should plan on 3–5 months, the length of Focus Lab's Structural Rebrand.
How much time does a rename add?

Months, and most of it is legal. The USPTO averaged 4.45 months to a first examination action and 10.03 months to final disposal in the first half of fiscal 2026. Clear the name with a trademark lawyer before it goes on anything, and ask whether you can launch before registration completes.
Should we rebrand before or after the fundraise?

It depends on how crowded your category is and which round comes next. If you've raised the Series A and you're pointing at a Series B, rebrand now; if you're pre-PMF, don't. The full decision is in rebrand before or after a fundraise.
Why do rebrands decay after launch?

Because nobody left a system behind. We call it brand entropy: about eight months after launch, the deck stops matching the site and engineers start inventing components. A design system with a named owner prevents it, and the cost guide covers what that costs.
Is a fast rebrand lower quality?
Only when a long process gets squeezed into fewer weeks. A sprint built for weeks keeps the craft and limits the scope. If your date is too close for the full scope, cut surfaces, not craft.
What should we have ready before a rebrand starts?

A date, such as the Series B announcement, and the one or two people who will sign off. Bring the opinion you hold about your market, the current deck, and customer proof you can publish. Book the decision-makers' calendars before kickoff, because their availability sets the pace more than the designers' does.

Use the next week to work through the first five rows. Treat it as a focused review, not a promise that approvals or security work will finish in seven days. Assign one owner to each gap and give them a specific output.

Write one company description. It should name the customer, the problem, and what your product does differently. Compare it with your homepage, LinkedIn profile, and deck. The wording can fit each channel; the audience and promise should agree. If sales says "AI infrastructure for banks" while the homepage says "productivity for everyone," fix that before choosing a typeface.

Make customer proof usable. Ask for permission to publish a name, the use case, and a result the customer can substantiate. If no metric is available, a specific, approved account of the work is better than a made-up percentage. If names are confidential, label the example as anonymous and explain only what you're allowed to share.

Write the security page with the person who owns security. State your actual audit status, explain data handling at an appropriate level, and show how buyers can request further documentation. Link to a subprocessor list if you maintain one. An audit in progress should be described as in progress; a page cannot supply controls the product lacks.
Put accountable people on the about page. Names, roles, relevant experience, and a working contact route help a buyer understand who is behind the product.

Read the deck beside the website. Check the category, customer, product names, use cases, and proof points. Keep details appropriate to each audience, but resolve contradictions. Give your AE a current deck template and assign someone to maintain it when the product changes.
When does the brand and website need deeper work?

Deeper work earns its cost when the evidence exists but the presentation obscures it. Your best customer story is buried. Product pages need a founder to translate them. The sales deck explains a clear market position that the homepage never mentions.

For Sully's 2025 website project, we approached the work as a sales-enablement problem. Hospital executives needed to understand how the AI workflows fit their operations. The job was to make those workflows understandable before the demo, through product pages and explainers.

The system after launch matters too. For Greptile's 2025 rebrand and design system, we worked across brand, product, website, and sales assets. The point for this checklist is consistency: the buyer shouldn't have to reconcile a different company story at each touchpoint.

Give your team reusable components, deck templates, and a clear owner for updates. Otherwise, each new page becomes another decision about how the company should present itself. That drift is what we mean by brand entropy.
When should you use DIY, a freelancer, or a subscription?
Choose the smallest engagement that fixes the actual gap. A full rebrand is hard to justify when the positioning works and three pages need clearer copy.

items: Still finding product-market fit? Keep the site simple and update it yourself. Account for template, hosting, and tool costs. Don't hire us to lock in a story you're still testing.

Strategy settled and a narrow set of pages to execute? A freelancer can be a better fit. Our planning estimate is $2–8k for a limited execution scope, not a market-wide quote or a budget for a complete enterprise brand system.

Need a recurring queue of design assets? Consider a subscription such as Designjoy. We would choose that model for defined production requests when the direction is already clear. Confirm that the scope matches the work you need.

Need a large stakeholder process? Look for a partner staffed for research, workshops, and approvals across that group. Our process works best with a founder and a small decision-making team. Our comparison of tech branding agencies names studios built for that, including Focus Lab and Motto.

body.x: If deals are stalling and you don't know whether presentation is the blocker, start with why enterprise deals stall after a good demo. A rebrand is the wrong fix for missing product capabilities or unresolved security requirements.
When a partner like PIXELUP LABS wins

We're a fit when you're funded, moving upmarket, and need brand, website, and sales materials built around a clear position. How we know: our work includes Sully, Bland, Reducto, CTGT, and Greptile's 2025 rebrand and design system. Our brand sprint is $15k; brand + website is $25–40k; retainers start at $6k/mo. Brand sprints take two to four weeks and brand + website six to eight, with scope and approvals agreed upfront. Compare the scopes on our Contra services page. If the budget doesn't fit, the cost guide by stage covers other routes.
FAQ
How do I make my startup look more credible to enterprise buyers?

Make the company easy to evaluate: clear positioning, relevant customer proof, accurate security information, an identifiable team, and consistent website and sales materials. Start with missing answers and contradictory claims. Bring in design help when the presentation prevents buyers from understanding the evidence you have. Our list of design agencies for AI startups compares ten studios that do that work, with prices.
My competitor rebranded and now we look outdated, what do we do?

Check whether buyers are struggling to understand your product or trust your company. If they are, fix those gaps around your own position rather than copying the competitor's new look. For the broader timing decision, read rebrand before or after the raise.
How much does it cost to look enterprise-ready?

Content fixes may need no additional agency budget if your team has the capacity and evidence. A focused freelancer engagement has a different scope from our $15k brand sprint or $25–40k brand + website project. Budget separately for security work, audits, and any product changes buyers require.
Can we get enterprise-ready without a full rebrand?

Often, you can improve credibility through clearer copy, better customer proof, and focused page updates. A full rebrand becomes relevant when the name, positioning, or identity no longer fits the company you're building. Neither approach replaces actual operational readiness.
How fast can this happen if a big deal is already in the pipeline?

Start with the buyer's unanswered questions and identify which your team can resolve this week. Our brand sprints take two to four weeks and brand + website projects six to eight, but those are design timelines. Customer permissions, security reviews, and procurement approvals follow their own dependencies.
How do we know if our website is the thing making us look early-stage?

Ask someone who resembles your buyer to review the homepage and explain what you sell, who it's for, and what evidence they found. Then ask your AE which questions keep coming up after prospects visit the site. Use that feedback to identify specific changes; a quick visual impression alone won't tell you why a deal stalled. That fits a global company buying campaign reach, multi-market coordination, media, and enterprise delivery. It is the wrong comparison for a Series A founder choosing a small senior studio.
Use Dentsu when network scale is part of the deliverable. Use the six studios above when the job is bounded.
Character SF is not character.studio
There is also a current studio at character.studio. It is not the San Francisco agency Dentsu acquired.

The current Character is a two-person design and technology studio working across product, websites, and brand. It embeds fractionally with Seed to Series B teams and charges hourly rates plus equity.
It can be a good alternative if you want a design partner inside the company and the boundaries between brand, product, and website should stay open. It is not a continuation of Character SF.
When the old Character model is still the right model
The old Character model still makes sense in three situations.
Brand experience is broader than the website. Packaging, retail, campaigns, product, and brand all need to feel like one company.
Stakeholder confidence is part of the purchase. A recognized portfolio and larger network reduce internal risk for some boards and marketing leaders.
The company can use the scale. If the launch spans markets, media, CRM, commerce, and brand experience, Dentsu's network is built for that coordination.
A Series A startup usually needs less surface area, fewer meetings, and a team that can turn one sharp market opinion into a brand before the next board meeting.

For the wider decision, use our B2B AI and tech branding-agency comparison. If the product is the hard part, use the AI startup design-agency comparison. For another prestige product studio, see the Metalab alternatives guide.
FAQ
What are the best Character SF alternatives in 2026?

For funded startups, the strongest active alternatives are PIXELUP LABS for a fast B2B or AI brand-and-site engagement, C42D for transparent startup packages, Focus Lab for deeper B2B transformation, Ramotion for brand plus product systems, basement.studio for digital craft, and Smith & Diction for verbal and visual identity. Dentsu Creative is the direct organizational successor.
Is Character SF still in business?

Character SF was acquired by Dentsu in 2018. Its current LinkedIn company profile says “Now DENTSU CREATIVE.” We could not verify a current independent Character SF offer or price in September 2026, so this page treats Dentsu Creative as the successor and does not pretend the old studio is still a standalone option.
How much does Character SF cost?

There is no defensible current independent Character SF price. The studio did not disclose financial terms when Dentsu acquired it, and current public sources do not publish a standalone project minimum. Any precise 2026 Character SF range should be treated as an estimate unless it comes from a current proposal.
Is character.studio the same as Character SF?

No. Character SF was the San Francisco branding agency founded in 1999 and acquired by Dentsu. character.studio is a current two-person design and technology studio that works across product, websites, and brand through hourly rates plus equity.
What are the best basement.studio alternatives for a Series A startup?

Choose by the missing capability. PIXELUP or C42D if positioning, identity, and website must ship as one bounded project. Focus Lab if research and stakeholder alignment are heavier. Ramotion if product UI is central. Smith & Diction if verbal identity matters more than development.
Which Character SF alternative is cheapest?

Based on published project floors, PIXELUP's brand sprint starts at $15,000 and C42D starts at $20,000. basement.studio has a reported $10,000 directory minimum, but it does not publish an official package and the scope may not include strategy. The cheapest number is useless until the deliverables match.
Which alternative is best for brand and product design together?

Ramotion is the clearest fixed-package option because it publishes separate brand, product, and team-extension offers. The current character.studio is another fit if you prefer an embedded fractional relationship with hourly fees plus equity. PIXELUP fits when brand and website lead and product design is supporting scope.
Should a Series A startup hire a prestige agency?

Only if prestige, stakeholder management, or global rollout is part of the job. Most Series A teams should spend $25,000 to $60,000 on the smallest senior team that can solve positioning, identity, and the launch surface. The startup rebrand cost guide maps the sensible range by stage.
The bottom line
Do not build a shortlist from an outdated directory.
Character SF did strong work and still appears in old lists. In 2026, the useful decision is between the Dentsu network and active independent teams with current scopes.

What does a B2B branding agency do?

A B2B branding agency decides what a company stands for in its market, then builds the words and visuals that carry it: positioning, messaging, visual identity, and a brand system the in-house team can run. For a B2B AI or tech startup, the audience is a buying committee, not a single shopper.

That committee is what separates B2B tech branding from consumer branding. A consumer brand has to win one person in a few seconds. A B2B tech brand has to survive an engineer checking every claim, a VP repeating the pitch to a CFO, and a procurement lead asking whether the company will still exist in three years.

The hardest version is a product that is hard to explain. Most AI startups we meet describe themselves in the same words as their closest competitors, so the first deliverable is a sentence, not a logo.
On Workers.io, that sentence was the "agents to workers" reframe. On Sainapse, it was the IIRA positioning framework. The identity came after the opinion.
A new logo is not the flex. A buyer who can repeat what you do to their boss, correctly and unprompted, is.

A B2B branding agency is not a performance-marketing shop, a logo marketplace, or a product-UX team. If the interface is the hard part rather than the story, MetaLab, entry 9 below, is built for that job.

Where it does not. MetaLab is product-led by design. A B2B AI startup needing a focused positioning, identity, and marketing-site sprint can buy more product capability, team, and time than the problem requires.

When should a B2B AI startup not hire a branding agency?
When the position is still moving, when the job is production, when the real problem is demand, or when the only reason is an agency's client logos.

items: Do not hire a branding agency while the product, ICP, or category is still moving. A brand amplifies a position. If the position changes next quarter, the expensive system becomes an expensive artifact.

Do not hire one if the strategy and Figma are locked. You need production, and a freelancer or design subscription will be cheaper. Our agency vs freelancer vs subscription guide maps that decision with current prices.
Do not hire one to solve a demand problem. Design makes each impression land harder. It does not create impressions. If nobody is reaching the page, hire the team that fixes distribution.
Do not hire a $100,000 agency because the board likes its client logos. At Series A, the unused process is usually the most expensive line item in the proposal.

body.x: How should a B2B SaaS company choose a web design agency?

Name the job before you name the agency. Most B2B SaaS website problems are one of five: an enterprise-perception gap, a sales-enablement gap, a website-operations bottleneck, a monthly queue of pages and tests, or a product that loses users after signup. Each one points to a different shortlist.
“We raised, moved upmarket, and still look seed-stage”

The problem starts in positioning and perception, so shortlist PIXELUP LABS or Everything Design. Choose PIXELUP LABS for a smaller senior team and a compressed schedule. Choose Everything Design when a longer diagnosis and Webflow program fits the plan. Choose Ramotion for a full new brand at a published package price, if you can give it a quarter.
“We hired an enterprise AE and the site is now part of every deal”

Start with the buyer journey, proof, security, use cases, and sales enablement. PIXELUP LABS fits the fast brand-and-site reset, Bop fits a broader web, copy, and SEO project, and Huemor fits a larger custom redesign.
“Marketing cannot publish without engineering”

That is a website-operations problem. Shortlist Webstacks for composable architecture and a dedicated website product team. Shortlist Refokus when the target platform is Webflow and the migration or creative-development bar is unusually high.
“We need landing pages and CRO every month”

Shortlist Overpass, because a subscription matches continuous demand better than buying a new project every quarter. If the need also includes paid media, SEO, ABM, and RevOps, add TripleDart. If you would rather keep the team that ran your reset, our retainer starts at $6k/mo.
“People sign up, then fail to reach value”
Stop redesigning the homepage. Shortlist UX Studio or another product UX team. The problem is activation, onboarding, or the application itself.
When should a B2B SaaS company not hire a web design agency?
When the company is pre-PMF, when the job is one campaign page, when strategy and Figma are already locked, or when the real problem is traffic or activation.

items: If you are pre-PMF: your ICP, category, and product are still moving. A fixed brand and large site will turn into expensive debris after the next pivot.
If you need one campaign page: hire a good freelancer or a focused Webflow developer. A full agency process will cost more than the problem.

If the strategy and Figma are locked: hire an implementation partner, such as TripleDart's Figma-to-Webflow team or BRIX. Do not pay a strategy-led studio to agree with decisions it is not allowed to change.
If the real problem is traffic: hire for distribution. A redesign can make each visit clearer. It cannot manufacture an audience.
If the real problem is activation: fix the product. A sharper homepage does not repair a confusing onboarding flow.

body.x: Seven questions to ask a SaaS web design agency before signing
Ask every SaaS web design agency on your shortlist these seven questions before you sign.

items: Who writes the copy? “We collaborate with your team” often means your marketer writes it after the wireframes are approved.
Who builds the production site? Ask whether development is in-house, subcontracted, or handed back to you.
Which CMS are you recommending, and why? “We always use Webflow” is not an answer to a business question.
Can marketing create a new use-case, integration, comparison, or industry page without a developer? Ask to see the actual editor experience.
Which people from the pitch will work on the account? Agency logos do not ship websites. Named people do.
What happens after launch? Get the support window, ownership, documentation, training, and retainer terms in writing.
Which result did the website cause? Traffic, pipeline, fundraising, and conversion can move for ten reasons at once. Be suspicious of the agency that claims all of it.

body.x: FAQ
What is the best web design agency for a B2B SaaS company?

It depends on the job. PIXELUP LABS fits funded B2B SaaS companies repositioning for enterprise quickly, Webstacks fits mature teams that need composable architecture and website operations, and Bop Design fits one project combining design, development, copy, and SEO. Overpass fits monthly design and Webflow work, and Huemor fits a larger custom rebuild. Pick by scope and operating model, not the prettiest portfolio.
How much does a SaaS website design agency cost in 2026?

Public offers on this list range from Overpass's £1,950-a-month design rate card to Huemor's $50,000-$100,000 custom redesign and Ramotion's $85,000-$120,000 for a new brand with a small website, with Bop Design starting at $25,000. PIXELUP LABS charges $25,000-$40,000 for brand plus website, while Webstacks and Refokus quote enterprise work privately. Compare what is included, not just the number: positioning, copy, development, migration, training, and post-launch support.
How long does a B2B SaaS website redesign take?

PIXELUP LABS runs brand plus website in 6-8 weeks, Everything Design publishes 8-14 weeks, Ramotion 8-16 for most web projects, Huemor 12-16, and Bop Design 16-20. Webstacks cites 90-120 days for current client websites in its ServiceTitan case study, and TripleDart puts Figma-to-Webflow builds at 1-6 weeks when the design is already done. Timelines stretch with stakeholder count, copy, migration, and how quickly your team supplies decisions and content. If the brand is changing too, see how long a startup rebrand takes.
What should a SaaS web design agency include?

At minimum: discovery, information architecture, responsive design, production development, analytics, QA, CMS setup, and training. If the positioning is unclear, the scope should also include messaging and copy, as Bop Design's $25,000 starting package does. For a mature SaaS site, ask for reusable product, solution, industry, integration, comparison, pricing, case-study, and trust-page patterns rather than a pile of one-off pages.
Who maintains a B2B SaaS website after launch?

Either your own marketing team or the agency on a retainer. Webstacks keeps a dedicated website product team on the account, Overpass works as a monthly subscription, and PIXELUP LABS offers a retainer from $6k/mo. If your team will run the site, write CMS training, documentation, and a support window into the contract, as Everything Design does with its Webflow hand-offs.
Do we need a SaaS specialist or is a general web agency fine?

A generalist is fine when the product is easy to explain and the site is small. A B2B SaaS specialist becomes useful when the site must serve self-serve users and enterprise buyers, or explain several products to a long buying committee. It matters most when you publish integrations and comparisons at scale. Huemor's SaaS page, for one, designs for both self-serve and sales-led flows.
Should a SaaS website use Webflow, WordPress, or a headless CMS?

Use Webflow when a design-led marketing team needs control without maintaining a custom frontend. Use WordPress when the team already has a strong WordPress operation and needs its plugin or publishing ecosystem. Use a headless or composable stack when the site spans many products, regions, integrations, or content systems and the organization can support the engineering complexity. Platform follows the operating model.
Should positioning, copy, design, and development come from one agency?

Usually, if all four are changing. One team, such as Everything Design or PIXELUP LABS, removes the handoff where strategy gets diluted into wireframes and copy gets forced into a layout. Split the work when one layer is already strong. If positioning and copy are locked, a specialist build partner can be faster and cheaper than restarting discovery with a full-service agency.
What is the difference between SaaS marketing-site design and SaaS product UX?

The marketing site gets a prospect to understand, trust, and try or contact the company. Product UX helps the user reach value after entering the application. The two influence each other, but they require different research, workflows, and specialists. PIXELUP LABS, Bop, and Overpass lean toward the marketing site, while UX Studio is the clearest product-UX specialist on this list.
Which agency is best for a sales-led SaaS website?

Overpass explicitly focuses on sales-led software companies and sells website work by the month, with CRO as its own service. PIXELUP LABS fits a funded sales-led company whose larger problem is enterprise perception and positioning. Bop fits a broader web, copy, and SEO project. The best choice depends on whether the immediate bottleneck is the story, the launch, or continuous conversion work.
Which agency is best for a product-led SaaS website?

Choose a team that understands the whole path from homepage to signup, pricing, onboarding, and activation. Huemor covers self-serve and sales-led flows in larger website engagements. UX Studio is stronger when the problem continues inside the product, as in its six-week UXfolio activation project. Webstacks fits a mature PLG company that needs its marketing site and content system to support many routes into the product.
When should a SaaS company redesign its website?

Redesign when the product, buyer, category, or GTM motion has changed enough that the current site tells the wrong story. A new enterprise tier, a move from PLG to sales-led, several new product lines, a painful CMS, or a brand that no longer matches the company are real triggers. Sainapse's trigger, after seven years in market, was an identity that had become fragmented and hard to explain. Boredom with the homepage is not a trigger.
Should a Series A SaaS company hire an agency or an in-house designer?

Hire an agency when the need is immediate, spans positioning through production, and requires several specialties for a short period. Hire in-house when design is continuous and close to the product every week. Many need both in sequence: an agency for the reset, then an internal designer to run it. Our agency vs freelancer vs subscription vs in-house guide compares the real costs, from $27 an hour to $240k a year.
How do we know whether our SaaS website is hurting enterprise sales?

Look for the same objections after a good demo: buyers cannot repeat the value, security information is hard to find, the site and deck tell different stories, and the company looks much earlier than it is. Procurement is a decision-maker in 53% of business buying cycles and engages from the start, per Forrester's 2026 research, so those gaps surface early. The website rarely kills a deal alone, but it can confirm every risk a buyer already fears. See why enterprise deals stall after a good demo and how to look enterprise-ready.
Can a web design agency improve SaaS conversion rates?

It can remove friction, clarify the offer, improve routes to demo or trial, strengthen proof, and create a system for testing. It cannot guarantee conversion because traffic quality, product, pricing, sales follow-up, brand awareness, and market conditions also change the result. With more than 60% of business buyers now running a trial, per Forrester, the handoff from site to trial can matter as much as the homepage. Ask agencies to separate what they shipped from what they merely observed afterward.
Do we need an AI-specialized agency for an AI SaaS website?

Not automatically. You need a team that can make a complex product legible without turning it into vague “AI-powered” marketing language. An AI-specialist roster matters when model trust, technical buyers, or an invisible product are central to the story. For that narrower decision, use our best design agencies for AI startups comparison, which covers MetaLab, basement.studio, Lazarev, and seven more.
The bottom line
Do not hire a B2B SaaS web design agency because its portfolio looks expensive.
Hire it because its operating model matches the problem.
PIXELUP LABS fits the funded B2B company whose product has moved upmarket faster than its brand and website. For every other job, the TL;DR table at the top of this page names the agency and why.
If you cannot state the job that clearly, do not book ten agency calls yet. Diagnose the problem first.
If your problem is the fast upmarket reset, our current services and pricing let you disqualify us before a call. If another agency here fits the job better, hire them.

We wrote this list and we put ourselves first. Read our entry with that in mind: here is our price, here is what we are bad at, and here are four studios that beat us for specific jobs.

Where it doesn't. That same process costs time, and the top of their range goes past Metalab's floor. They are a brand studio first, so product design depth is thinner than Clay's or Metalab's.

Pricing signal. Clutch lists a $25,000+ minimum, rechecked September 25, 2026. Focus Lab's own FAQ puts Focused Branding at around $15,000–$50,000 over 1–3 months and a Structural Rebrand at around $75,000–$350,000 over 3–5 months. Its retainers start at $5,000 a month for design execution.
Verdict. Hire Focus Lab for a B2B rebrand that has to survive a committee.

basement.studio homepage, captured September 25, 2026 · basement.studio
What it is. A boutique studio in Mar del Plata, Argentina, founded in 2018, known on design Twitter for 3D, motion, and websites that get screenshotted.
Where it shines. The lowest real entry price here, and the highest ceiling on visual ambition per dollar.

Where it doesn't. Craft-led execution, not positioning and messaging strategy. Their Clutch profile is not yet reviewed, so you are buying on portfolio rather than verified outcomes. And motion-forward work can fight the exact thing an enterprise buyer wants, which is a company that looks like a safe bet.
Pricing signal. Reported Clutch figures are a $10,000+ minimum and $100–149/hr. We could not verify these on a live profile.
Verdict. Hire basement.studio for a site that has to be beautiful and loud, not for the brand argument underneath it.
Studios we left out, and why

The filter for this page: senior-led studios that can plausibly do Metalab's job for a funded startup. Four categories did not pass, and here is what they are instead. For the wider field, see our comparison of AI design agencies, which adds product studios like Lazarev and Punchcut, and our list of B2B branding agencies for AI and tech startups.

items: Designjoy ($4,995/mo) and ManyPixels (from $699/mo). Subscriptions, and good ones. They buy throughput, not a positioning-led rebrand. Designjoy is one person, Brett Williams, on a 48-hour average turnaround. Neither is a Metalab substitution, and neither pretends to be.

Superside. Scaled production from $15,000 a month on an annual term, and Superside says most teams start between $20,000 and $50,000 a month. That is an in-house-team replacement, not a brand studio. Our Superside alternatives breaks down its pricing.
Pentagram. A genuine peer in craft, and the opposite of cheaper.

Offshore generalists billing $25–49/hr. One Metalab alternatives list that ranked for this query earlier in 2026 sent readers to studios in that rate band. At $25 an hour you are not buying a cheaper Metalab, you are buying a different product. That can be the right call, and it belongs on a page about outsourcing.

body.x: What should you ask before signing with a Metalab alternative?
Three questions tell you whether a lower price buys the same job or a smaller one. Get the answers in writing, next to the quote.

items: Who does the work, and for how much of their week? Metalab staffs teams "100% dedicated to a single client." Ask what the alternative offers instead.
What is in the price? Brand only, brand plus website, or product design too. A Clutch minimum is a floor, not a quote.
What do you keep after launch? Components, templates, and documentation your team can edit. A logo folder is not a system.

body.x: If an answer is vague, so is the price.
When Metalab is still the right choice
Four situations where we would tell you to go pay them.

items: Your product is the hard part, and it's big. A multi-surface application with real complexity, research needs, and engineering handoff. 475+ products shipped with fully dedicated teams is a different machine than a 7-person studio.
You need a household name for a board or an acquirer. "Metalab did it" carries weight in rooms you are not in. That is worth money, and it is honest to say so.
Consumer scale. Slack, Coinbase, Uber, Headspace. If your surface is consumer and the user count is enormous, that is their home turf and not ours.
You have the budget and the calendar. $100k+ and a few months, with no launch date forcing the issue. Take the longer engagement. It is better.

body.x: The reverse is also true, and it is why this page exists. If you raised a Series A eight months ago, your site was built in Claude Code over a weekend in 2024, and your first enterprise AE starts in three weeks, a four-month engagement is not a better version of what you need. It is the wrong purchase.
That is the trap here. The most expensive studio is not the safest choice, it is the choice with the longest gap between deciding and shipping.
David Walsh, CEO of Limelight, has bought most of the options on this page across twelve years. His summary after hiring us:
"over the last 12 years, I've worked with: Big-name website agencies. 'Top-rated' Upwork freelancers. Designers with huge followings. And none came close."
He posted it unprompted and named all four people who did the work. Big-name is a category, not a guarantee.

What are the best Metalab alternatives for startups?

For funded B2B startups: PIXELUP LABS ($15–40k by scope, 2–8 weeks by scope), Clay ($50k+), Ramotion ($50k+), Focus Lab ($25k+), basement.studio ($10k+), and Character (hourly plus equity) as an embedded partner. Match the choice to the job, not the reputation: product complexity points to Clay, systems to Ramotion, committee politics to Focus Lab, a deadline to us.
How much does Metalab cost?

Metalab publishes no prices. Their Clutch profile lists a $100,000+ minimum project size and DesignRush lists $50,000 and up, both rechecked September 30, 2026. Assume six figures for brand plus product work, and months rather than weeks.
Is Metalab worth it?

Yes, if the brief matches. They have shipped 475+ products since 2006 and staff teams 100% dedicated to one client. At $100k+ over several months, the question is not quality. It is whether your stage can absorb the timeline.
Who is cheaper than Metalab?

Everyone on this list. basement.studio starts at $10,000, our work runs $15–40k by scope, Focus Lab's Clutch minimum is $25,000, and Clay and Ramotion both list $50,000 minimums, against Metalab's $100,000 Clutch floor. Cheaper is easy to find. Cheaper with senior taste and a real point of view is the hard part.
What studios are like Metalab at a Series A budget?

At $15–50k the realistic set is PIXELUP LABS, Focus Lab's lower tier, and basement.studio for web-only work. Clay and Ramotion are the step up at $50k+. Below $15k you are usually buying execution without strategy, which is fine if the strategy is already done.
Does Metalab work with AI startups?
Yes. They rebranded Windsurf in 2025 and their portfolio includes Midjourney and Suno. AI is one of the industries they name directly, alongside fintech, productivity, healthcare, and SaaS.
How long does a Metalab engagement take?
Metalab does not publish timelines, and fully dedicated teams point to months rather than weeks. For comparison, our brand sprint is 2 to 4 weeks, and brand plus website is 6 to 8.
Which studio should a funded startup pick for brand and product design?

Work backwards from your deadline and your decision structure. Deadline inside 8 weeks with one or two decision-makers: a boutique sprint studio, which is our lane. A quarter or more with a committee: Focus Lab. Designers embedded in your team for the long run: Character. A genuinely complex product surface at $50k+: Clay or Metalab.

title: Rebrand Before or After a Fundraise?
description: Should you rebrand before or after a fundraise? Use product-market fit, trust and growth to decide, with first-party insights from Greptile’s founder.

body.x: Don’t decide when to rebrand based on when the money hits the bank. Decide based on what is limiting the company.

Before product-market fit, usually wait on a full rebrand. After PMF, start fixing weak positioning and presentation when they hold back growth. If you are going upmarket, those gaps become harder to postpone.

When PIXELUP LABS first started working with Greptile, the company was roughly three people. It was a seed-stage startup building developer tooling with barely an interface beyond configuration and settings. Nobody expected sophisticated branding.
Finding a great design partner was still important to the founders.

In a conversation with me, Greptile’s founder explained why: he believed good design created enough economic value to justify the investment through customer trust, product appeal and recruiting. He wanted the outside of the company to reflect how much the team cared about what it was building.
That challenges the blanket advice to wait until after a raise. It also does not mean every three-person startup needs a full rebrand.
The real inflection point is when the quality of the company starts outrunning the way the company presents itself.
TL;DR

rows: Usually wait on a full rebrand. Keep the brand flexible.
Product is stronger than the way the company looks
Rebrand or redesign, depending on where the gap is.
Differentiate before more go-to-market spend amplifies sameness.
Fix credibility, narrative and website before they become sales constraints.
Series A raised and scaling toward Series B
Usually rebrand if the brand no longer represents the company.
Don’t expect branding to save it. Fix the underlying fundraising problem.

body.x: The funding round is the wrong trigger
Fundraising and rebranding often happen close together because a round can fund changes that were already needed.
The company starts hiring. The sales team targets larger accounts. The product serves a more demanding customer. A website built to explain an early idea now has to support a much bigger business.
Those changes create the need. The funding announcement gives the work a deadline.

This distinction matters because the same problem can show up before the money arrives. Greptile’s founders cared about design while the company was still tiny. Another startup might raise a Series A with a brand that already works well.
Neither should make the decision from the round alone.
The better trigger: your company has outgrown its brand
A startup outgrows its brand when what customers can see no longer reflects what the company can do.

The product has matured, but the website still describes the first version. The founder explains the difference clearly on calls, but the homepage could belong to any competitor. The company wants enterprise customers, but the site gives those buyers little evidence that it understands their needs.
Start by naming the gap.
If the positioning is clear and the execution has drifted, a refresh may be enough. If the company’s story has changed, a deeper rebrand may be needed.

rows: A confusing website with otherwise clear positioning
Positioning that no longer fits the product, buyer or category
Rebrand, including messaging and identity where needed

body.x: A refresh keeps the positioning and updates how it looks. A rebrand changes the argument itself, sometimes including the name.
If you can explain your difference out loud and your site does not say it, start there. New typography cannot do that job for you.

Greptile’s founder described a related ambition: making the outside of the product show the passion behind it. That is a useful standard for a startup brand. Does it represent the care and quality already there?
Before PMF: usually wait
Before product-market fit, your understanding of the customer and product may still change substantially.
An expensive identity built around today’s positioning can become the wrong identity after the next pivot. Keep the website clear, the product usable and the brand easy to change.
Do not hire PIXELUP LABS for a full rebrand if you are still figuring out what you sell, who needs it or why they would stay. Put the time and money into answering those questions.
That does not mean accepting confusing design. Fix onboarding that prevents people from using the product. Rewrite a homepage that nobody understands. Bring in a freelancer for a contained problem.
Greptile shows that a small team can deliberately prioritize design early. It does not establish that every seed-stage startup should buy the same scope of work.
The useful distinction is between improving what customers experience now and trying to perfect a brand around assumptions that are still changing.
After PMF: design moves much higher up the list
Greptile’s founder made his strongest point about what happens after product-market fit.
You have created something valuable for customers. Now you need to grow. In his view, that is when great design moves much higher up the priority list.
This gives startup branding after product-market fit a clearer purpose. You have something worth explaining, and more people need to understand why it matters.
The website needs to make that value easier to grasp. The brand needs to give buyers a reason to remember you. Recruiting materials need to help talented people see what they could build with you.
The round can help pay for that work. But the need may already exist.
What does good design actually buy you?
Greptile’s founder described several kinds of value. These are his beliefs and experience as a buyer of design services, rather than measured promises about what a rebrand will deliver.

Customer trust and appeal. He believes good design builds trust and draws people toward a product or company. Buyers cannot inspect every decision behind your software. They can see how clearly and carefully you present it.

A more intuitive product. His argument covered design broadly, including how the product works. A brand project alone cannot fix difficult workflows. If usability is the problem, product design belongs in the scope.

Recruiting and internal pride. He said talented, motivated people want to work on beautiful things. He also described the founder’s own experience: a more functional, intuitive product can be more enjoyable to work on.
A visible signal of care. His team wanted its external presentation to communicate the passion behind the product. Design gives people something visible from which to form that impression.
For us, the practical connection to growth is straightforward. Every campaign sends people somewhere. If they arrive at a generic or confusing website, more traffic does not resolve the confusion.
What we will not tell you is that a rebrand moves your conversion rate by some guaranteed number. If an agency promises to transform your product metrics in a two-week sprint, run.
If your market is crowded, you may need to move earlier
In a saturated category, sameness is the problem, and closing a round does not solve it. You raise, and then you are a funded company that still looks like the other forty.
The work starts with positioning rather than a logo.
Founders in crowded categories will rant for twenty minutes about why the incumbent’s approach is broken, and then their website says “the AI-native platform for modern teams.”
That gap is the whole job.
Explain who the product is for, what you believe the category gets wrong and how your approach changes the customer’s experience. Make an argument a buyer can understand and evaluate.
You may need to do this before a Series A. You may be able to do it yourself with a good writer or designer.
A crowded market is a reason to sharpen your story early. It is not automatically a reason to buy an entire new identity.
Series A to Series B: your brand has to carry a much bigger company
After Series A, the same brand may need to support enterprise sales, recruiting, launches and the next fundraise.

You hire the first enterprise account executive. A “Contact sales” tier appears on the pricing page. Prospects ask harder questions about implementation, support and whether you understand their business.
Your product may have good answers. Your website needs to help communicate them.

This is where Greptile’s founder’s point about growth becomes especially useful. Once you have something valuable and want to grow quickly, the quality of your external presentation deserves more attention.
A rebrand after Series A usually makes sense when the company has changed enough that the old brand is now getting in the way.
If the positioning remains accurate and the site supports the new sales motion, keep what works. Raising a round does not make a good brand obsolete.
But if every sales call begins by correcting the impression your website creates, the cost of waiting is already showing up in the work.
Going enterprise doesn’t mean becoming boring
Greptile deliberately rejected the idea that serving large companies required conservative, generic branding.
Its founder’s reasoning was simple: senior engineering leaders are still developers. They can appreciate interesting, opinionated design.
That is a useful correction for startups moving upmarket.
Enterprise credibility comes partly from helping buyers understand the product, assess the evidence and find answers to serious questions. None of that requires removing the company’s personality.
Looking mature does not mean looking generic.

A rebrand should make the company feel more intentional and credible while preserving what makes it recognizable. You can have a distinctive identity and a clear explanation of security, implementation and support.
Rebrand before the raise or after it?
Use the business problem to decide the timing, then check what you can afford.
Rebrand before fundraising when the gap is already holding you back
Start before the raise when you have product-market fit and the current positioning or presentation is becoming a constraint.
That might mean buyers cannot tell you apart, the product has materially outgrown the website, or an upmarket push needs a stronger story.

An upcoming launch or funding announcement can add urgency because more people will encounter the company. But attention alone does not justify a full rebrand. There should be something worth fixing before they arrive.
Scope the work to that problem. Sometimes positioning and a rewritten homepage are enough.
Rebrand after fundraising when waiting protects the business
Wait when a pivot is likely, cash is tight or the current brand is adequate for the next six to twelve months.
Also wait if you are trying to use design to solve a weak fundraising story. A better identity cannot establish demand, retention or a convincing market opportunity.

The Greptile founder suggested that design can contribute to an investor’s impression that a team cares deeply about its product. That is a limited signal. It cannot compensate for weak traction, team or market.
A rebrand will not save a round.
Once you have decided, work backward from the announcement
The close and the announcement are different events. The announcement may bring a concentrated burst of attention from buyers, candidates, investors and press.
If a rebrand is already justified, that can be a useful launch deadline.

Agree on scope, content, approvals and development before committing to the date. A signed term sheet is not cash in the bank, so the project should be affordable even if closing takes longer than expected.
If the window has passed, pick another real deadline: a product launch, a conference or the start of an enterprise sales push.
Who should actually do the rebrand?
Choose based on the work and the context it requires.

rows: One homepage, deck or other contained execution problem
Continuous product and design work inside the team
Brand, positioning and website changing together
Ongoing internal needs plus a larger project or extra capacity

body.x: Greptile brought design in-house relatively early and continued working with PIXELUP LABS afterward.

Its founder mentioned the volume of work, but his larger point was about depth. A partner becomes more useful as it learns what the company wants to become, what the product is trying to say and the principles behind it.
That accumulated understanding helps keep the work consistent and the story coherent.
The decision does not have to be agency versus in-house forever. You need someone close enough to the company to make good decisions, with enough capacity to deliver the work.
When a partner like PIXELUP LABS makes sense
Disclosure: we are a design studio, and this is the work we sell.
PIXELUP LABS makes sense when a B2B startup needs its positioning, brand and website to change together, with a team that can understand the product and carry that understanding through the work.

That could be a company going upmarket, a post-PMF team whose presentation has fallen behind, or a startup preparing for a launch that needs more than a homepage facelift. To compare us with other studios for that job, see our lists of B2B branding agencies and AI design agencies.
If you need one asset fixed, start smaller. If the company’s direction is still changing, keep the brand flexible.

We quote by engagement because scope drives the price. The starting point is deciding what needs to change and what is worth keeping. More about working with PIXELUP LABS. See our current services and pricing on Contra.
